newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes mostly lower despite exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes mostly lower despite exports.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mostly lower on a sharp drop in the KCBT and MGE markets, traders said.
"Kansas City December and Minneapolis got blasted, so that hurt us here," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
KCBT December ended six cents lower and MGE December dropped 4-1/4 cents.
Traders said the volume was thin throughout the day which left the market vulnerable for the late slide that mainly was triggered by local selling.
The late break occurred despite optimistic export news.
"We talk about no wheat business yet we continue to see nearly one-half million tonnes every week and I think it's very constructive," said Mark Cermak, of O'Connor and Co.
USDA Friday said the net export sales for wheat during the week ended November 7 totaled 474.9 million tonnes, above trade expectations for 300,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
Wheat also was underpinned by hints of a brighter export outlook with the European Union this week cutting back on the amount of subsidy for wheat exports.
Wheat closed 2-1/4 cents per bushel lower to 1/2 higher, with December up 1/2 at $3.97-1/4.
Wheat futures also were underpinned by indications of firmer French and Argentine wheat prices and U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman Friday indicated a "cooling off" of wheat export wars.
Glickman, in Rome for the U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit, said the EU was not using wheat export subsidies aggressively.
Paine Webber sold 1.5 million bushels of March and Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, sold one million December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 16,500 contracts, below the 20,207 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Refco Inc sold 300 December $4.80 puts at 8-1/2 cents, traders said.
Options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, below the 4,346 traded Thursday.
